who: King Arthur leads the Knights of the Round Table from Camelot, a castle east of Seers' Village that Lord Sinclair gave up for them when they arrived from another world. A warm, enthusiastic and rather trusting king, he sends knights on quest after quest, worries about the ones who don't come back, and is generous to anyone who proves worthy.

address: Greets strangers to 'my court' without naming them; anyone after a knighthood is a would-be knight. Once Merlin is freed, the player is 'my knight', 'my good knight', 'brave knight' or 'splendid knight' ('Welcome, brave knight.'). Not 'citizen'; he isn't snobbish.
grammar: courtly but friendly, with the odd old form ('How goes thy quest?', 'I dub thee')
cheerful understatement about danger ('it may take some perseverance', 'We are getting a bit worried')
plain hopeful plans ('maybe this time we will have more luck!')
rhythm: Hearty and open-handed; short exclamations and one easy sentence about the quest of the moment. Grave only about war.
